checkResults.note: Expo 57.0.9 / RN 0.86.2 / client 0.1.7 / iOS 26.3.1 sim / release artifact sha d7ba67eafd4a…; all identities recorded.

Clean release launch through the supported path (expo run:ios artifact via simctl); fresh signed-out boot witnessed on-device. Reaching this launch at all required the consumer-authored WebCrypto polyfill (finding 0137-a1expo-f1): without it the documented path dies at session establishment.

In-app email-code entry (guide auth/native-apps.md shape 1): /auth/request-code and /auth/exchange executed on-device; mailbox read host-side under admin custody and relayed as the user. Deep-link return: not required by this auth shape (fully in-app; no external browser hop) — recorded explicitly.

Initial authoritative rows rendered and independently verified; outsider denied (SNAPBACK_AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED); second-device (host protocol client) commit visible on-device ≤33-42ms after settlement over genuine server push. Steady-state caveat filed as 0137-a1expo-f7: the connection axis cycles live→stale (~2s reconnect loop) and the public retainable query blanks after the first cycle, so the chips read 'stale' even while deliveries land.

Background via Settings launch (inactive/background witnessed), second-device commit while backgrounded caught up on foreground; network loss (origin refusing) left rendered rows retained under a non-live connection fact, never relabeled live; reconnect returned live and a fresh commit flowed.

Cold process restart with the backend unreachable is clean (app-keychain bearer survived; app renders an honest 'backend unreachable' state and self-heals when the origin returns). Protected retained state is NOT CLAIMED on this carrier (guide: Online surface; default rqs store resolves to the in-memory arm, durable:false) — contract-sanctioned GAP vs A1's local-first floor, filed as 0137-a1expo-f3; the web arm cold-retains the public subset on the same contract.

Queue unclaimed on this carrier (Online surface) — and the documented offlineQueue opt-in cannot engage: Expo fetch rejects connection failures with a plain Error while the client's connectivity classification requires instanceof TypeError, so offline mutates surface raw transport errors and nothing queues (0137-a1expo-f2; node control with identical options and an explicit memory store queues {queued:true}). No ghost settlement (authoritative count unchanged; no offline-attempt clientKey ever committed); online server-refused edit surfaced structured and left rendered rows authoritative. Durable-across-restart additionally blocked by the missing on-device store arm (f3).

Evidenced defect (0137-a1expo-f4): rotation to a lesser-privileged principal blanks predecessor rows (correct) but rejects with AggregateError 'external bearer custody transition completed with lifecycle failures' carrying the expected denial, leaves the provider connection wedged 'disconnected', and rotate-back to the original authority NEVER re-subscribes the attached queries (device: all queries blank forever; node control: protected handle disconnected/0, public handle live-labeled with 0 rows) — recovery requires process restart. Logout itself is correct: rows blanked, app keychain custody cleared, relaunch boots signed-out with no predecessor data at rest (no durable client store exists on this carrier).

App terminated and uninstalled; simulator shut down; snapback dev stopped (origin refuses); receipted versioned reset-install (reset-installed, arm rows deleted, literal 3-site seed restored, workspace query denied post-cleanup); session bearers retired by the reset stream transition; admin/impersonation token files remain dev-local in the arm-owned external directory only. Hygiene note: expo-secure-store keychain entries survive app uninstall on the iOS simulator — the receipt run cleared them via simctl keychain reset pre-run and app logout in-run.

This receipt claims expo-ios simulator only (LLP 0064). Android: honest not-run — the host has an emulator binary and one AVD but no JDK, so expo run:android/gradle cannot execute; recorded in the capsule, no android receipt is minted.
